The drafting pass, done by hand in this session the way the news-draft skill does it in the owner's: one topic and one summary per item, written from the page behind the link. `pending` marks the items the owner approved this week and has not published yet. `week-of-codex` carries no summary on purpose: its page refused the fetch, and an undrafted item is a real state the page has to survive.

harness-evolution.summary: Dan McAteer argues that agents started working in late 2025 because the models and the harnesses around them improved at the same time, and their curves crossed. His forecast is that models keep absorbing harness features into their weights, engineers keep deleting what got absorbed, and what is left steers human attention instead of the model. It is the clearest statement so far of why a stack is worth measuring: the harness is the part that keeps changing.

traycer.summary: Traycer is an open-source workspace that runs Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor side by side over shared context, plans, and reviews. It brings your own agent, so it adds an orchestration layer without a second model subscription. It is the same bet as running two harnesses on one machine, made into a product.

claude-code-release.summary: Claude Code shipped v2.1.241 on August 23. The published notes say bug fixes and reliability improvements, and nothing more.
claude-code-release.note: Unlicensed release notes: our summary and the link, never the vendor's text.

codex-release.summary: Codex tagged 0.150.0-alpha.7, one of nine alpha builds in three days. The alpha train moves faster than the stable one, so a pinned Codex version can be a week behind the branch it was cut from.

opencode-release.summary: opencode v1.18.21 fixes two things that stop a session dead: a response that gives up when the model reports an unknown finish reason, and Vertex AI multi-region Gemini requests taking the wrong endpoints. The desktop build keeps file search results on screen while the next search loads.

gemini-cli-release.summary: gemini-cli cut v0.56.0 on August 19, then went straight back to nightlies. The release carries no notes of its own, only the compare link against v0.55.1.

onecli.summary: OneCLI launched on Hacker News as an open-source sandboxed agent harness aimed at teams rather than one developer. It reached 87 points and 31 comments. Team-shaped harnesses are now their own category, next to the single-user CLIs.

autolith.summary: Autolith is a terminal agent with a live Common Lisp runtime it can inspect, test, and extend while the conversation runs. It also claims recursive inference over corpora larger than the model window, plus portable conversations, memories, and checkpoints. It is a bet that an agent you can open up beats an agent that is faster.

cc-ab-effort.summary: A user reported that Anthropic enrolled Fable 5 sessions on Claude Code 2.1.236 and later into a server-side experiment that shrank the effort scale, so high behaved like low. The post says older versions and Opus 5 were left alone, and that the changelog did not mention it. Hacker News ran it to 196 points and 175 comments. Nobody in the thread had a way to check their own session.
cc-ab-effort.note: License class x: the official embed is the only thing we may re-serve.

deepseek-v4-flash.summary: DeepSeek shipped deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp, which takes images alongside text through the same OpenAI-compatible chat completions shape. Images arrive as base64, as a URL, or through the files API, and the format is detected from the file content rather than the name. It topped Hacker News at 496 points.

qwen-reverse-eng.summary: XDA gave Qwen 3.8 27B a reverse-engineering job the author assumed needed a frontier model, and it finished in thirty minutes. The point of the piece is the size: 27B runs on a well-specced laptop. It is the strongest single anecdote yet for putting a local model in a real stack.

qwen-overthinks.summary: Simon Willison rates Qwen 3.8 27B excellent and says it defaults to wildly overthinking. The model is Apache 2, vision-capable, and 27B, which is the size that fits a laptop. Qwen's own benchmarks put it above the closed-weight Qwen 3.7-Plus.

qwen-index.summary: Qwen 3.8 27B scored 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, matching GPT-5.6 Luna and landing one point behind GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek V4 Pro. Those two are 753B and 1.7T parameters. A 27B model at that score changes what a local tier is worth.

sol-ultrafast.summary: OpenAI previewed Ultrafast, an API service tier that runs GPT-5.6 Sol up to fourteen times faster on Cerebras hardware, at up to 750 output tokens per second. Speed is now a purchased tier rather than a property of the model.

gpt56-guide.summary: OpenAI published a builder's guide to GPT-5.6, covering model selection across the family and the new Responses API capabilities. The framing is cost per task rather than capability, which matches what the price cut on Sol suggests.

opus5-incoherence.summary: A long-running claude-code issue collects reports that Claude 4.7, 4.8, 5.0, and Fable increasingly fall into repetitive rhetorical tics and ignore explicit style instructions. It reached 189 points on Hacker News. The bug is open, and the thread is the closest thing to a public record of the drift.

fable5-longhorizon.summary: Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's frontier model for reasoning, coding, vision, and multi-day agentic work. It is served through Claude, the API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry. Multi-day is the claim worth watching, because it is the one a stack can actually measure.

gemini-changelog.summary: Gemini 3.7 Flash reached general availability as Google's workhorse model for coding and agents. Google reports substantial gains in software engineering, web development, and agentic workflows, at an introductory price through December 31, 2026.
gemini-changelog.note: CC BY 4.0: the changelog text itself is re-servable with attribution.

agents-md.summary: The request for Claude Code to read AGENTS.md is the loudest open issue in the repository, at 375 points on Hacker News. Codex, Amp, and Cursor already standardize on the file. Every stack that runs two harnesses keeps two instruction files today, and that is the cost the thread is arguing about.

mcp-roadmap.summary: The Model Context Protocol maintainers published a roadmap for the next specification releases. The priorities are agentic messaging primitives, one hardened HTTP-native transport, agent identity with enterprise security, and better SDK ergonomics. Transport unification is the one that will move real servers.

wayfinder-skill.summary: Latent Space interviewed Matt Pocock about /wayfinder, a skill for projects whose end state is not clear yet. It charts the fog of war as a map of decisions instead of a plan. His AI Skills for Real Engineers project is the distribution behind it.

promptot.summary: PromptOT gives teams typed prompt blocks, version history, evaluations, per-environment deployment, and one-click rollback through an API. The argument is that a prompt change alters production behavior as much as a code change, so it deserves the same machinery.

week-of-codex.note: Undrafted. The page refused the fetch, so the drafting run left it and the next run re-attempts it.

more-than-review.summary: Simon Willison names the skill that makes coding agents pay: instruct confidently, then verify confidently. Reading every line is one way to verify and not the best one. It is the shortest statement of why the review step, not the generate step, is where a stack differs.

claudette.summary: NoBuzz is a Claude Code skill that rewrites Claude's last response to strip the listicle voice. It hit 352 points and 235 comments on Hacker News, which is a lot of feeling about prose style. Skills as post-processors on your own agent's output are a pattern worth noting.

vomit.summary: Vomit runs a second, smaller model over Claude 5's output to clean it up, including stripping generated comments. It reached 303 points and 297 comments. Two models in one pipeline, one to produce and one to trim, is the same shape as a router.

stop-making-tuis.summary: Thomas Ptacek argues that coding agents made a usable GUI so cheap that a terminal UI is no longer the sensible default for a personal tool. Simon Willison agrees and points at two vibe-coded macOS task bar apps he uses daily. The claim is about cost, not taste.

harness-gap.summary: AniC_dev argues a competent human on a basic harness with almost any capable model beats Fable 5 running autonomously. The post puts human steering and workflow design above the gap between frontier models. It is the counter-argument to picking a stack by benchmark.

sol-price-cut.summary: GPT-5.6 Sol dropped to $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output, a twenty percent cut, with cached input at $0.40. The context window is 1,050,000 tokens and the effort scale runs from none to max. A price move on the default frontier tier resets every cost estimate built on it.

bedrock-10x.summary: Codex running natively on AWS Bedrock has no explicit cache controls, so sessions rewrite the cache and the bill lands around ten times higher than expected. The issue is closed, and it reached 148 points on Hacker News. The same session on the same model costs a different amount depending on the route.

codex-rate-limit.summary: OpenAI traced unexpected Codex rate-limit drain to image-heavy long sessions, Computer History, and automatic conversation-title generation. Limits were reset the following afternoon. Two of those three are features the user never asked to spend on.

memory-prices.summary: Memory prices are up 500% in twelve months, with 128GB DDR5 kits at ten times their lowest recorded price. The shortage has run unabated since February. Every local-model plan that starts with buy more RAM now has a different budget.

model-routing.summary: Glean's chief executive explains why model routing became a core part of enterprise deployment: frontier prices are high, open-weight models are close enough, and human feedback at scale improves the routing. Stripe bought OpenRouter for over $7B in the same month. A stack with a router in it now has to say which model actually served the work.

local-llm-dumber.summary: A Level1Techs post runs experiments on why a model you host feels worse than the one the lab hosts: quantization, sampler defaults, and the gap between your inference stack and the reference implementation. It reached 417 points on Hacker News. The measured answer is that the weights are rarely the problem.

self-hosted-factory.summary: Jake Saunders built a self-hosted sandboxed agent pipeline that took one prompt to a repository, a written app with tests, green CI, a provisioned Postgres, and an HTTPS deploy without a second message. The write-up is honest about the almost in the title. It is the clearest end-to-end picture of what a sandboxed agent stack costs to run.

smolvm.summary: Simon Willison tested smolvm 1.8.3 as a sandbox for untrusted Python and JavaScript and found it holds: hardware-isolated VMs rather than shared-kernel containers, offline images, no-network execution, CPU and memory limits, and storage quotas. Cold starts land around 0.6 to 1.5 seconds and warm runs around 50 milliseconds. He ran the testing itself with Claude Fable 5 in Claude Code.

watch-claude.summary: Mike Kasberg used Claude to write a watch face for a $27 PineTime running open-source firmware. The interesting part is not the watch, it is that embedded work with unfamiliar firmware is now a weekend that starts from a drawer.
